To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the fruit yield of chilli was positively and significantly correlated with number of fruits, fruit weight, plant spread, pericarp color in red and green fruits, pericarp in oleoresin, capsaicin content in green and red fruits, powder yield, days to first and last picking and plant height.

fruit yield is positively and significantly associated with the number of fruits plant1, fruit weight pericarp thickness, powder yield, days to first pick, plant height, fruit length and capsaicins in green and red fruits and color in the oleoresin.
fruit yield had a significant and positive correlation with number of fruits per plant, fruit weight and plant spread, days first picking and plant spread.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new chilli varieties that have high yield, high quality and high resistance to diseases.
the genetic variability, character association and path analysis in chilli genotypes.
the development of chilli genotypes with higher yield and better oleoresin quality.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the selection based on these characters would improve the fruit yield and other traits.

the selection of genotypes for fruit yield should be based on the selection of number of fruits plant1, fruit weight pericarp thickness, fruit length, days to first fruiting, fruit weight and color in oleorecin.
the present study is a good starting point in developing a suitable selection criteria for the improvement of fruit yield in chilli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the selection of superior chilli genotypes based on fruit yield, number of fruits plant1 and fruit weight would be rewarding.
, the selection for yield should be done by taking into account the number of fruits plant1, fruit weight powder yield and days to first picking.
, the present study would help in the selection of genotypes with high yield and other important characters for the commercial cultivation of chilli pepper in India and other countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of path analysis and correlation analysis is very useful in the selection of traits for the improvement of yield in chilli pepper.
we have developed a set of chilli germplasms which could be utilized for further genetic studies.

the use of path analysis is an efficient method to understand the interrelationship between yield and its component traits and also to select the best traits for the improvement of fruit yield in chilli.
